subject: Ectotherm under different vegetation cover configurations (with DEB model on)

messages.author: 5481ac51bfcf2936
messages.subject: Ectotherm under different vegetation cover configurations (with DEB model on)
parts:
Hi all,


I have seen in previous posts that to simulate the vegetation cover I should modify the sun angle, wind factor, besides altering the max/min of shade. However, I want to model the canopy cover and further run the ectotherm model with the DEB model turned on to assess the consequences of different cover configurations (e.g before and after wildfires) on the ectotherm’s life history and physiology.


So my questions are: 


Since I am using the DEB model, is the cap parameter (presence of organic matter on the ground) related to the food available for the ectotherm, or it just account for physical properties to model the micro-environments?


By changing the parameter X (food density), does it change the proportion of food that the ectotherm "eats" ?


For comparative purposes, I would also like to compute the average growth rate over a given period (e.g. 5 years). Is there a straightforward way to do that?


Finally, these procedures can be equally applied for the micro_ncep and micro_aust?


Sorry for so many questions. Any suggestion will be highly appreciated.


Thanks,

Rodolfo

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Ectotherm under different vegetation cover configurations (with DEB model on)
parts:
Hi Rudolfo,

The 'cap' parameter is altering the thermal properties of the surface as would be the case if there was a reasonable amount of low-conductivity organic matter. I found this was necessary to capture soil temperature in places where there is some vegetation present, e.g. a layer of grass. It's explained further in

Kearney, M. R., Shamakhy, A., Tingley, R., Karoly, D. J., Hoffmann, A. A., Briggs, P. R., & Porter, W. P. (2014). Microclimate modelling at macro scales: a test of a general microclimate model integrated with gridded continental-scale soil and weather data. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 5, 273–286. https://doi.org/doi: 10.1111/2041-210X.12148
and of course it's in the help files for the microclimate model e.g. ?micro_global
cap = 1, organic cap present on soil surface? (cap has lower conductivity - 0.2 W/mC - and higher specific heat 1920 J/kg-K)
It is completely unrelated to food.
The parameter X is a DEB parameter. It sets the available food but this may be at a level above what is limiting for the animal depending on its maximum foraging rate. I would strongly advise that you avoid using the DEB model without fully understanding what it's doing. It is a steep learning curve for sure but the NicheMapR package hopefully makes learning it easier, because it provides you with something to play with, and there's a vignette about it in the package to get you started but the DEB book is the place to go to properly learn it, and the deblab.
The outputs of micro_global, micro_ncep, etc. are all identical in structure and the ectotherm model is set up by default to feed in the microclimate data from these runs if you've stored it in a list called 'micro'. So yes, no matter which microclimate function of the 'micro_' style functions in NicheMapR, the ectotherm will run from them. It doesn't make sense to run the DEB model unless you're running a daily time-step. The micro_global function by default runs the middle day of each month so to make that function run daily you'd need to set 'timeinterval' to 365 (and nyears to greater than one if you want to run multiple years).

All the best,
Mike
